questions.question: Why do ultraviolet (UV) rays appear brighter or more intense when they strike a glass surface?

options.text: because glass completely absorbs UV rays
because glass reflects UV rays more than visible light
because the wavelength of UV rays is very long

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**because glass reflects UV rays more than visible light**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reflection of UV Rays by Glass:**

 
 
• Glass has a unique property of reflecting **ultraviolet (UV) rays** more efficiently compared to visible light.
 
• This phenomenon makes UV rays appear **brighter and more intense** when they strike a glass surface.
 
 
 
• **Absorption of UV Rays:**
 
 
• Ordinary glass typically absorbs a significant portion of UV rays, especially those with shorter wavelengths. However, the UV rays that are not absorbed are reflected, contributing to their apparent intensity. This is why the statement "glass completely absorbs UV rays" is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength of UV Rays:**
 
 
• UV rays have **shorter wavelengths** than visible light. This shorter wavelength interacts differently with glass compared to longer wavelengths of visible light.
 
• The statement "the wavelength of UV rays is very long" is incorrect because UV rays are characterized by their short wavelengths.
 
 
 
• **Glass Producing Colored Light:**
 
 
• Glass does not inherently produce colored light when UV rays strike it. The interaction of UV rays with glass involves reflection and absorption, not the production of colors. Hence, the statement "glass produces colored light" is also incorrect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties of Ultraviolet (UV) Rays:**

 
 
• UV rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths ranging from **10 nm to 400 nm**, shorter than visible light but longer than X-rays.
 
• They are categorized into three types: **UVA (315–400 nm)**, **UVB (280–315 nm)**, and **UVC (100–280 nm)**.
 
• UV rays are largely absorbed by the Earth's **ozone layer**, but some UVA and UVB rays reach the surface.
 
 
 
• **Interaction of UV Rays with Glass:**
 
 
• Ordinary glass blocks most UVB and UVC rays but allows a portion of UVA rays to pass through.
 
• Special types of glass, like **quartz glass**, can transmit more UV rays, while laminated or coated glass is designed to block UV rays effectively.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Glass in UV Protection:**
 
 
• Glass is often used in windows and eyewear to block harmful UV rays and protect individuals from exposure.
 
• Special coatings on glass can enhance its ability to reflect or absorb UV rays, making it suitable for use in **automobiles, buildings, and protective gear**.
 
 
 
• **Reflection Coefficient:**
 
 
• The reflection of UV rays by glass is determined by its **reflection coefficient**, which varies based on the angle of incidence and wavelength of the radiation.

questions.question: Radioactivity refers to the rate at which a particular nuclide undergoes radioactive decay. Which of the following units is used to measure radioactivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Curie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Curie (Ci)** is a unit used to measure radioactivity, named after **Marie and Pierre Curie**.
 
• One Curie corresponds to **3.7 × 10¹⁰ disintegrations per second**, representing the decay rate of radioactive isotopes.
 
• It is primarily used in fields such as **nuclear medicine, radiology, and environmental monitoring**.
 
• The Curie is considered a large unit, and smaller units such as **millicurie (mCi)** or **microcurie (μCi)** are often used in practice.
 
• The International System of Units (SI) uses the Becquerel (Bq) for measuring radioactivity, where **1 Curie = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Becquerels**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Radioactivity**: It is the phenomenon of spontaneous emission of particles or electromagnetic radiation from the nucleus of unstable atoms.
 
• **Roentgen (R)**: It is a unit of exposure used to measure ionizing radiation, particularly in air, but does not measure the decay rate.
 
• **Becquerel (Bq)**: The SI unit for radioactivity, defined as **one disintegration per second**.
 
• **Applications of Radioactivity**: Used in medical imaging (e.g., PET scans), cancer treatment (radiotherapy), energy generation (nuclear power), and archaeological dating (carbon dating).
 
• **Safety Measures**: Handling radioactive materials requires protective equipment, proper shielding, and adherence to radiation exposure limits to minimize health risks.

questions.question: If a boy covers a distance of 20 metre in 4 minutes with a force of 600 N, then the power consumed by the boy is:

• Time is taken by the boy (t) = 4 min ⇒ 240 s
 
• Force (F) = 600 Newtons
 
• We know that work = Force × distance

= F × d

= 600 × 20

W = 12000 N-m (Newton-Meter)

 
• Power consumed by the body (P) = Work/Time

P = 12000/240

P = 50 Watts

 
• Therefore, the power consumed by the boy is 50 Watts.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is an acid-base conjugate pair?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**NH₄⁺ and NH₃**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **acid-base conjugate pair** consists of two chemical species that differ by a single proton (H⁺).
 
• **NH₄⁺** (ammonium ion) acts as an **acid** because it can donate a proton (H⁺).
 
• **NH₃** (ammonia) acts as a **base** because it can accept a proton.
 
• When **NH₄⁺** loses a proton, it becomes **NH₃**, and when **NH₃** gains a proton, it becomes **NH₄⁺**.
 
• This reversible exchange of a proton makes them an ideal **acid-base conjugate pair**.
 
• Such pairs are critical in understanding the behavior of acids and bases in chemical reactions, particularly in the context of the **Brønsted-Lowry theory.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **H⁺ and O²⁻**__

 __
 
• This is not an acid-base conjugate pair because **H⁺** is a proton, and **O²⁻** is an oxide ion. They do not differ by a single proton.
 
• However, oxide ions (**O²⁻**) can act as a strong base and react with protons (**H⁺**) to form water.
 
 
 
• **H₂O and H₂O₂**__
 __
 
• **H₂O (water)** and **H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide)** are not an acid-base conjugate pair because they differ by more than one atom or structure rather than by a single proton.
 
• **H₂O₂** is a strong oxidizing agent and has different chemical properties compared to **H₂O**.
 
 
 
• **HCl and Cl₂**__
 
 
• **HCl (hydrogen chloride)** is a strong acid, but **Cl₂ (chlorine gas)** is a diatomic molecule and does not act as a base in this context.
 
• These two species are not related by the gain or loss of a single proton.
 
• **HCl** is commonly used in various industrial and laboratory applications, including pH adjustment and chemical synthesis.

questions.question: An object of 5 kg is lying at rest. Under the action of a constant force, it gains a speed of 3 m/s. The work done by the force will be _________.

The correct answer is __**22.5 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Work-energy theorem: It states that the sum of work done by all the forces acting on a body is equal to the change in the kinetic energy of the body i.e., Work done by all the forces = Kf - Ki
 
• W = (1)/(2)m{v²} - (1)/(2)m{u²} = {bf{Δ }}K
 
 
• Where v = final velocity, u = initial velocity and m = mass of the body
 
 

CALCULATION__**:**

Given,

Mass (m) = 5 kg

Final Velocity (v) = 3 m/s 

Initial velocity (u) = 0 m/s

According to the work-energy theorem,

⇒ Work done = Change in K.E

questions.question: To do a certain work, A and B work on alternate days, with B beginning the work on the first day. A can finish the work alone in 48 days. If the work gets completed in 11(1)/(3) days, then B alone can finish 4 times the same work in:

Work done by A = (16/3) ÷ 48 = 1/9. Remaining work done by B = 1 − 1/9 = 8/9.

B finishes 8/9 work in 6 days ⇒ B finishes full work in (6 × 9)/8 = 27/4 days.

B finishes 4 times the work in (27/4) × 4 = 27 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 days.**

questions.question: Anu fixes the selling price of an article at 25% above its cost of production. If the cost of production goes up by 20% and she raises the selling price by 10% then her percentage profit is (correct to one decimal place):
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **initial cost price** be 100.

Initial **Selling Price** = 100 × 1.25 = 125.

New **Cost Price** = 100 × 1.20 = 120.

New **Selling Price** = 125 × 1.10 = 137.5.

New **Profit** = 137.5 − 120 = 17.5.

Profit% = (17.5 ÷ 120) × 100 ≈ 14.6%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.6%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial markup = 25%, CP increase = 20%, SP increase = 10%.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11075ca7438a51530953af2ab1d21b7dccf766bb102a42c4e2bb658de131f893.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP₁)** = 100.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP₁)** = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125.

⇒ **New Cost Price (CP₂)** = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120.

⇒ **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 125 + 10% of 125 = 125 + 12.5 = 137.5.

⇒ **Profit** = 137.5 − 120 = 17.5.

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (17.5 ÷ 120) × 100 = 1750 ÷ 120 = 14.583%.

⇒ Rounding to one decimal place, we get **14.6%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.6%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Base Value for Profit

Profit is always calculated on the **actual cost price** unless specified otherwise. Formula: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Markup and Selling Price

**Marked Price** is the price at which SP is fixed initially before any subsequent changes or discounts.</p

questions.question: The average of 20 numbers is 32. If two numbers are 29 and 31, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct up to two decimals)?

Net increase in average = 4 ÷ 18 ≈ 0.22.

New average = 32 + 0.22 = 32.22.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (n₁) = 20

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e23ddbd157f7b74cefb3fe2f5452474bdfb2ca3a5c4b071e7e959d7b59bc0354.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of the two removed numbers = 29 + 31 = 60

⇒ Sum of the remaining numbers = 640 − 60 = 580

⇒ Total remaining numbers = 20 − 2 = 18

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of First n Natural Numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Effect of Replacement on Average

When a value x is replaced by y, the New Average = Old Average + (y − x) ÷ Total Count.

Weighted Average

For two groups with averages A₁, A₂ and counts n₁, n₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 8 : 9. After 9 years, this ratio will become 19 : 21. C is 3 years younger to B. What is the present (in years) of C?

Ratio Balancing Method

To solve age ratios quickly, multiply the ratios by the difference of the other ratio to make the parts corresponding to time equal.

Linear Equation in Ages

Product of Two Numbers

questions.question: 40 litres of milk are kept in a container. 4 litres of milk were removed from this container and replaced with water. This procedure was performed two more times. How much milk does the container now hold?

Remaining milk = 40 × (1 − 4/40)³ = 40 × (9/10)³

Remaining milk = 40 × 0.729 = 29.16 litres.

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Initial amount of milk = 40 litres

Amount removed and replaced by water = 4 litres

Total number of times the process is performed = 1 (initially) + 2 (more) = 3 times

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/939c49c25063f8c5ad2599123e1f6600a94b41a5a54e872418a609568e8c09a5.png]

⇒ Milk left = 4 × 72.9 / 10

General Replacement Formula

Ratio of Ingredients

The ratio of the original liquid to the replacing liquid (water) after n operations is [P × (1 − R/P)ⁿ] : [P − (P × (1 − R/P)ⁿ)].

questions.question: If a + b + c = 2, a² + b² + c² = 26, then the value of a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For expressions of the form **a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc**, use the direct formula:

**Value = (a + b + c) ÷ 2 × [3(a² + b² + c²) − (a + b + c)²]**

⇒ Value = (2 ÷ 2) × [3(26) − (2)²]

⇒ Value = 1 × [78 − 4] = 74

**∴ The correct answer is 74.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of terms: **a + b + c = 2**

Sum of squares: **a² + b² + c² = 26**

**Formula Used:**

1. (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)

2. a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − (ab + bc + ca))

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0cea21d4a09e8d46ca1180ca359e2f347f09783cbaf6f2474fc38ef3445922ee.png] 

**Calculations:**

First, find the value of (ab + bc + ca):

⇒ (2)² = 26 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 4 = 26 + 2(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = 4 − 26

⇒ 2(ab + bc + ca) = −22

⇒ ab + bc + ca = −11

Now, substitute the values into the **cubic identity**:

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 2 × [26 − (−11)]

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 2 × [26 + 11]

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 2 × 37

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 74

**∴ The correct answer is 74.**

**__Additional Information__**

Special Case (a + b + c = 0)

If the sum of the three variables is zero, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Alternative Form of Cubic Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 1/2 × (a + b + c) × [(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²].

Condition for Zero Result

The expression a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc equals zero if either a + b + c = 0 or a = b = c.</p

questions.question:
Find the median of given data.

{13, 2, 5, 18, 6, 3, 6, 7, 8, 11, 17}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given **11 terms** in ascending order:

2, 3, 5, 6, 6, **7**, 8, 11, 13, 17, 18

Since the number of terms (n = 11) is **odd**, the median is the middle-most term:

Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term = 6th term = **7**

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given Data:** {13, 2, 5, 18, 6, 3, 6, 7, 8, 11, 17}

**Total number of observations (n):** 11

**Formula:**

When n is odd, Median = value of ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th observation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1e7c7808ff90785d75bab2f245970c6bfcd61c2155e59a4ad82a198cc55b048.png] 

Step-by-step calculation:

⇒ Arrange the data in ascending order: 2, 3, 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 11, 13, 17, 18

⇒ Count the total number of observations, n = 11

⇒ Since n is odd, the median is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term.

⇒ Median term position = (11 + 1) ÷ 2 = 6th term

⇒ The 6th term in the sorted list is 7.

⇒ Therefore, the median of the given data is 7.

**Why other options are incorrect:**

⇒ **Option (1) 6:** This is the mode of the dataset (since 6 appears twice, which is the highest frequency), not the median.

⇒ **Option (2) 6.5:** This would be the median if there were 12 terms and the middle terms were 6 and 7, but here we have an odd number of terms (11), so the median must be a single middle value, which is exactly 7.

⇒ **Option (4) 8:** This is the 7th term in the sorted list, which is not the middle-most term.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If the number of observations (n) is even, the median is the average of the (n ÷ 2)th and ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th terms: Median = [Value of (n/2)th term + Value of (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

Mean is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations: Mean = (∑ xᵢ) ÷ n.

Mode

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A dataset can have one mode, more than one mode (multimodal), or no mode at all.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.</p

questions.question: Reema sold 48 articles for Rs. 2,160 and suffered a loss of 10%. How many articles should she sell for Rs. 2,016 to earn a profit of 12%?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the formula: (Price₁ ÷ (Articles₁ × (100 − Loss%))) = (Price₂ ÷ (Articles₂ × (100 + Profit%)))

2,160 ÷ (48 × 90) = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

2,160 ÷ 4,320 = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

1 ÷ 2 = 2,016 ÷ (n × 112)

n × 112 = 4,032 ⇒ n = 4,032 ÷ 112 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 articles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling Price (SP₁) = Rs. 2,160 for 48 articles, Loss = 10%. Target Profit = 12% for SP₂ = Rs. 2,016.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb50910d649c70a26133b8b670bcb6ef24d900ded7bcbbc6725c531fe18ca83a.png] 

⇒ SP of 1 article = 2,160 ÷ 48 = Rs. 45

⇒ CP of 1 article = 45 × (100 ÷ 90) = Rs. 50

⇒ Required SP of 1 article for 12% profit = 50 × (112 ÷ 100) = Rs. 56

⇒ Number of articles for Rs. 2,016 = 2,016 ÷ 56 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 articles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in P&L

When solving for multiple articles, it is often easiest to find the **Cost Price (CP)** of a single unit first.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise in the question.</p

questions.question: Rewa has some hens and some goats. If the total number of animal heads is 100 and the total number of animal feet is 348, then what is the total number of goats with Rewa?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume all 100 animals are hens (2 feet each).

Total feet would be: 100 × 2 = 200 feet.

Excess feet count: 348 − 200 = 148 feet.

Each goat has 2 extra feet compared to a hen (4 − 2 = 2).

Total goats = 148 ÷ 2 = 74 goats.

**∴ The correct answer is 74 goats.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of heads = 100

Total number of feet = 348

**Formula Used:**

H + G = Total Heads; 2H + 4G = Total Feet (where H = Hens, G = Goats)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a9d82d02c3d89590492be49a5ee185644947907dd993e8cc53a18a412885bebd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average feet per head = 348 ÷ 100 = 3.48

⇒ By Alligation method, Ratio of Hens to Goats = (4 − 3.48) : (3.48 − 2)

⇒ Ratio (Hens : Goats) = 0.52 : 1.48 = 13 : 37

⇒ Total units = 13 + 37 = 50 units

⇒ 50 units = 100 animals

⇒ 1 unit = 2 animals

⇒ Total Goats = 37 × 2 = 74

**∴ The correct answer is 74 goats.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Formula for 4-legged animals

Number of 4-legged animals = (Total feet − 2 × Total heads) ÷ 2. This is derived from linear substitution.

Weighted Average Principle

The mean value (3.48) always lies between the two extremes (2 and 4). The closer the mean is to one extreme, the higher the proportion of that category.

System of Linear Equations

Problems involving two variables and two conditions (like heads and feet) can always be solved using the substitution or elimination method.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the number of coins of 25 paise, 50 paise, Rs. 2 and Rs. 5 is 5 ∶ 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 1, respectively. If the total amount of the coins is Rs. 285, then the difference between the number of 25 paise and Rs. 5 coins is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Value ratio = (5 × 0.25) : (4 × 0.50) : (3 × 2) : (1 × 5) = 1.25 : 2 : 6 : 5

Sum of ratio parts = 1.25 + 2 + 6 + 5 = 14.25

Value of 1 unit = 285 ÷ 14.25 = 20

Difference in count between 25 paise and ₹5 coins = (5 − 1) × 20 = 4 × 20 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80 coins.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of number of coins (25p : 50p : ₹2 : ₹5) = 5 : 4 : 3 : 1

Total amount = ₹285

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = ∑ (Denomination × Number of coins)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a461adecdff269258a160d642bd3240a28be1ff053bdcc806b9c2d4fe694a49.png] 

Let the number of coins be 5x, 4x, 3x, and 1x.

Total value in ₹ = (Number of 25p coins × 0.25) + (Number of 50p coins × 0.50) + (Number of ₹2 coins × 2) + (Number of ₹5 coins × 5)

⇒ (5x × 0.25) + (4x × 0.50) + (3x × 2) + (1x × 5) = 285

⇒ 1.25x + 2x + 6x + 5x = 285

⇒ 14.25x = 285

⇒ x = 285 ÷ 14.25

⇒ x = 20

Number of 25 paise coins = 5x = 5 × 20 = 100

Number of ₹5 coins = 1x = 1 × 20 = 20

Difference = 100 − 20 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80 coins.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

Always ensure all denominations are in the same unit (either all in paise or all in rupees) before calculation. 1 Rupee = 100 Paise.

Value vs Count Ratio

If the ratio of values is given as V₁ : V₂, the ratio of the number of coins is (V₁/D₁) : (V₂/D₂), where D is the denomination.

Combined Ratio

For three or more items, the total amount is ∑(Ratio Part × Denomination) × Constant = Total Money.

questions.question: From the top of an upright pole 24√3 feet high, the angle of elevation of the top of an upright tower was 60°. If the foot of the pole was 60 feet away from the foot of the tower, what tall (in feet) was the tower?

Here, h = 24√3 feet, d = 60 feet, and θ = 60°

H = 24√3 + 60 × tan(60°) = 24√3 + 60√3 = 84√3 feet

**∴ The correct answer is 84√3 feet.**

**Given:**

Height of pole (AB) = 24√3 feet

Distance between pole and tower (BD) = 60 feet

Angle of elevation (θ) = 60°

Let CD be the height of the tower and AB be the height of the pole.

⇒ tan 60° = CE ÷ AE

⇒ √3 = CE ÷ 60

⇒ CE = 60√3 feet

Total height of the tower (CD) = CE + ED

⇒ CD = 60√3 + 24√3

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking upwards at an object.

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

Relation between Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation of point A as seen from B is equal to the angle of depression of point B as seen from A because they are alternate interior angles.</p

questions.question: What is the ratio of the simple interest earned on a certain amount at the rate of 21% per annum for 8 years to that earned on the same sum at the same rate for 21 years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since the Principal (P) and the Rate of Interest (R) are the same for both cases, Simple Interest (SI) is directly proportional to Time (T).

SI ∝ T (when P and R are constant)

Ratio of Interest = Ratio of Time = T₁ : T₂

Ratio = 8 : 21

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 21.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P₁) = Principal (P₂) = P

Rate (R₁) = Rate (R₂) = 21%

Time (T₁) = 8 years

Time (T₂) = 21 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c45a3bcbe90770e4fb8fe374cf4c2e6d80720303b94252baef7dbf293cf6b880.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (P × 21 × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (P × 21 × 21) ÷ 100

⇒ Required Ratio = SI₁ : SI₂

⇒ Ratio = [(P × 21 × 8) / 100] ÷ [(P × 21 × 21) / 100]

⇒ Ratio = (P × 21 × 8) ÷ (P × 21 × 21)

⇒ Ratio = 8 ÷ 21

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 21.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality in SI

Simple interest is directly proportional to Principal, Rate, and Time individually when the other two factors remain constant.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total interest percentage for the entire period in SI is simply (Rate × Time)%. For example, 21% for 8 years is 168% of Principal.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In SI, interest is only calculated on the initial principal. In CI, interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.</p

questions.question: The average weight of three men is increased by 4 kg when one of them, whose weight is 100 kg, is replaced by another man. What is the weight of the new man?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New Weight = Replaced Weight + (Total Number × Change in Average)

Here, Replaced weight = 100 kg, Number of men = 3, Average increase = 4 kg

New man weight = 100 + (3 × 4)

New man weight = 100 + 12 = 112 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 112 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of men = 3

Weight of the man replaced = 100 kg

Increase in average weight = 4 kg

**Formula Used:**

Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + (Total persons × Increase in average)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d65e192926b7d37d807de350ebc81218453bf307c99244d8e0f9dadebb2c92d1.png] 

⇒ Total weight of 3 men = 3 × Average weight (A)

⇒ Let the weights of the men be M₁, M₂, and 100 kg.

⇒ (M₁ + M₂ + 100) ÷ 3 = A

⇒ (M₁ + M₂ + New Man) ÷ 3 = A + 4

⇒ M₁ + M₂ + New Man = 3A + 12

⇒ Since M₁ + M₂ + 100 = 3A, then M₁ + M₂ = 3A − 100

⇒ (3A − 100) + New Man = 3A + 12

⇒ New Man = 3A + 12 − 3A + 100

⇒ New Man = 112 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 112 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Replacement Rule

When one person is replaced, New Value = Old Value + (Total Count × Increase) or New Value = Old Value − (Total Count × Decrease).

Average of Group

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations. If the average increases, the incoming value must be greater than the outgoing value.

Effect of Adding a Member

When a person is added (not replaced), the total count increases. New Total Weight = (Old Average × Old Count) + New Member Weight.</p

questions.question: What is the simplified form of the expression (1+x)(1+x²)(1+x⁴)(1+x⁸)(1-x)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the telescoping pattern of the identity (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b².

Each pair of terms doubles the power of x: (1 − xⁿ)(1 + xⁿ) = 1 − x²ⁿ.

The sequence starts with power 1 and ends with power 8.

The final simplified power will be the highest power in the product multiplied by 2.

Highest power is 8, so final result is 1 − x⁸ × ² = 1 − x¹⁶.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 − x¹⁶.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given Expression: (1 + x)(1 + x²)(1 + x⁴)(1 + x⁸)(1 − x)

Formula: (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

⇒ Rearranging the terms to group conjugates:

⇒ [(1 − x)(1 + x)] × (1 + x²) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x²) × (1 + x²) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ [(1 − x²)(1 + x²)] × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x⁴) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ [(1 − x⁴)(1 + x⁴)] × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x⁸) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ 1 − (x⁸)²

⇒ 1 − x¹⁶

**∴ The correct answer is 1 − x¹⁶.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares Identity

The algebraic identity (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² is fundamental for simplifying products of binomial conjugates.

Exponents Rule

When raising a power to another power, the exponents are multiplied: (xa)b = xa × b.

General Telescoping Form

The general product (1 − x)(1 + x)(1 + x²)(1 + x⁴)...(1 + x²ⁿ) simplifies to 1 − x²ⁿ⁺¹.</p

questions.question: A train travelling at 44 km/h crosses a man walking with a speed of 8 km/h, in the same direction, in 15 seconds. If the train crosses a woman coming from the opposite direction in 10 seconds, then what is the speed (in km/h) of the woman?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Same direction) = 44 − 8 = 36 km/h = 10 m/s.

**Length of Train** = 10 × 15 = 150 m.

**Relative Speed** (Opposite direction) = 150 ÷ 10 = 15 m/s = 54 km/h.

**Woman Speed** = 54 − 44 = 10 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed of **Train** (ST) = 44 km/h, Speed of **Man** (SM) = 8 km/h, Time to cross man (t₁) = 15 s, Time to cross **Woman** (t₂) = 10 s.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Relative Speed × Time; 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd2083a0d412cbc6bb24e793c486d799ce20ed99beca4358c07dac9511962fec.png] 

⇒ Relative speed with man = 44 − 8 = 36 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/s = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s

⇒ Length of train (L) = Speed × Time = 10 × 15 = 150 m

⇒ Let the speed of woman be **x** km/h. Relative speed (opposite) = (44 + x) km/h

⇒ Length = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 150 = (44 + x) × (5/18) × 10

⇒ 15 = (44 + x) × 5/18

⇒ 270 = 220 + 5x → No, simpler: 15 × 18 / 5 = 44 + x

⇒ 54 = 44 + x

⇒ x = 10 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 10 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. In the **opposite direction**, it is S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Moving Object

The distance covered while crossing a person is equal to the **length of the train** itself, regardless of the person's speed.</p

=> a = 3 × b → **Eq. (1)**

**2)** After 5 years, she will be twice as old as Akanksha.

=> a + 5 = 2 × (b + 5) → **Eq. (2)**

**From eq. (1) put the value of a in eq. (2)**

=> 3b + 5 = 2 × (b + 5)

=> 3b + 5 = 2b + 10

=> 3b - 2b = 10 – 5

=> b = 5

**This value of b put in eq. (1)**

=> a = 3b

=> a = 3 × 5 = 15

**Hence, the present age of Radha is “15” years.**
